attacks.claim: The cost math mixes units. 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens is a daily figure, so $1,140 is the daily input cost, not the monthly one. Over 30 days input is about $34,200 (more on 61M-line peak days), roughly 23x the $1,500/month budget. The output figure has the same error: $7 is per day, about $207/month.
attacks.evidence: "Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140 ... Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget." while section 3 gives "38M lines/day average"

attacks.claim: The staffing math assumes 100% availability. The context says on-call and interrupt work averages 50% of both engineers' time, so real capacity over 6 weeks is about 6 eng-weeks against 12 planned. The schedule will slip about 2x, or quality work (eval, hardening) will be cut. The plan has no buffer.
attacks.evidence: "both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks)" vs. context "on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time"

attacks.claim: Per-window payloads are not sized against model context limits. The average is about 4,400 lines per service per 5-minute window, or roughly 264k tokens, and it is far larger for busy services and peak days. The plan has no sampling, dedup, or pre-aggregation step, so windows will be truncated or fail. This is also the cause of the cost problem.
attacks.evidence: "every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM"; "forwards every application log line"

attacks.claim: The launch gate is statistically weak and may not be feasible. With 40 incidents, a 5% misleading cap allows only 2 misleading summaries, and the commander grading is subjective. The plan does not say that 5-minute-window logs for those past incidents are still retained and replayable, and it gives no basis for the MTTR 47 to 30 minute target.
attacks.evidence: "Eval set from last 40 incidents"; ">= 70% useful, <= 5% misleading"

attacks.claim: Untrusted log content goes into an LLM prompt, and the output is posted to PagerDuty. A log line containing injected text could produce misleading summaries during an incident. The plan has no mitigation, although summaries are advisory.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: prompt-injection handling or output sanitization for the PagerDuty auto-comment

attacks.claim: The plan depends on a single LLM vendor (Corvid) and has no fallback or abstraction layer. A vendor outage means no summaries during incidents.
attacks.evidence: "Model: Corvid-mini"; ABSENT: fallback or degradation plan
